clue.text: Go in for canvassing, returning a Conservative Tyneside politician

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the first three pieces, a plus Conservative plus Tyneside, from back to front

parts.note: NE, the North East of England, is the region round the Tyne
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A political campaigner reports on canvassing for a Tory candidate in Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A, C and NE into ENCA. 'Canvassing' in the definition means living under canvas, not seeking votes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch tents and live under canvas is to settle into a camp, so going in for canvas living is exactly that.

clue.text: Rash needing antiseptic back on it somehow

indicators.note: back says the antiseptic word is read in reverse

parts.note: antiseptic means free of germs, pure

indicators.note: somehow suggests the two little words are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A rash needs antiseptic put back on it somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PURE into ERUP; 'somehow' turns ON IT into TION.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak of spots on the skin is a rash, a medical sense of the word.

clue.text: Limit the EU's means of intervention in farming

definitions.meaning: a ceiling or upper limit, as on spending

definitions.text: the EU's means of intervention in farming
definitions.meaning: the Common Agricultural Policy, by which the European Union supports farmers

explanation.surface: A complaint that EU farm intervention should be limited.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceiling on spending is a limit, and the initials name the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Union.

clue.text: Moon's plain when plugged by inadequate poet

indicators.note: plugged by says the second word is stuffed into the first

parts.note: a mare is one of the dark plains on the moon's surface
low means poor or inadequate

explanation.surface: A lunar plain is filled in by a second-rate poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' seems to describe the poet but supplies LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan dramatist and poet, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Some game's shape transformed by six-footer

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of shape are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: an ant is an insect, and insects have six feet

explanation.surface: A shape is altered by some six-footed creature in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' turns SHAPE into PHEAS. 'Six-footer' sounds like a tall man but means an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Game here means birds shot for sport and food, and this bird is a classic example.

clue.text: Whale with black crest which one may cross with a little effort

definitions.text: which one may cross with a little effort

parts.note: the humpback is a species of whale
B is the pencil abbreviation for black
a ridge is a crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A whale with a black crest that one may cross with some effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeply arched bridge, common over British canals, takes a little effort to walk or drive over.

clue.text: Additional info that's essential to gladden dataholics

indicators.note: essential to means forming the inner part of, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: Extra information is just what data lovers need to be happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential to' points into GLADDEN DATAHOLICS, where the letters run across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are items added at the end of a book or document, so additional material.

clue.text: Youth after a benefit setting about head of careers

parts.note: the dole is unemployment benefit

indicators.note: about says the setting word goes round the single letter

parts.note: a scene is a setting, as in a play

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of careers

explanation.surface: A young person on benefit is set to see a careers adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: The teenage years between childhood and adulthood are a person's youth.

clue.text: Fruit — take two tiny pieces alternately topped and tailed

indicators.note: the first copy loses its top letter and the second its tail letter
take two means the word for tiny pieces is written twice

parts.note: atoms are tiny particles

explanation.surface: Instructions to trim two small pieces of fruit at either end.
explanation.walkthrough: ATOMATOM loses its first A and last M.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a berry, this salad staple is a fruit.

clue.text: Sweet packet often found crumpled around car back

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters are placed round the turned car
crumpled says the letters of packet often are scrunched into a new order
back says the word car is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A sweet wrapper is often found crumpled behind the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' turns PACKET OFTEN into PONTEF...TCAKE, and 'back' turns CAR into RAC in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pontefract cake is a small round liquorice sweet from Pontefract in Yorkshire.

clue.text: As a fresh play, not fully developed without theatre backing

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: unformed means not yet fully shaped or developed

indicators.note: backing says the word for theatre is read in reverse

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A critic says a new play is underdeveloped and lacks a theatre to back it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'backing' turns the theatre word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand-new play has never yet been staged, so it has not been put on before an audience.

clue.text: Medical Officer suffering setback about hospital unit

indicators.note: about says the turned-round doctor goes round the hospital letter
suffering setback says the abbreviation is turned backwards

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A medical officer suffers a career setback over a hospital unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering setback' turns MO into OM; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the SI measure of electrical resistance, so it is a unit.

clue.text: Deterioration in market produce for show

indicators.note: in says the decay word sits inside the selling word

parts.note: to tout goods is to push or market them
rot is decay or deterioration

explanation.surface: Produce on a market stall is deteriorating and on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something out and display it, often a tired excuse, is an idiom for producing it for show.

clue.text: Winger in the open air flew off?

parts.note: outside means in the open air
left means departed, flew off

explanation.surface: A bird in the open air flies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' suggests a bird, but it is the football position.
explanation.definitionFit: In old football formations this was the attacking player on the left wing, so a winger.

clue.text: Author's inclination to keep clear of all charges

indicators.note: to keep says the inclination word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination or talent
net means after all deductions and charges have been taken off

explanation.surface: A writer is inclined to keep clear of legal charges.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Bennett, the playwright, and Arnold Bennett, the novelist, both fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett and Arnold Bennett are well-known English writers, so the surname names an author.

clue.text: Switch positions around article opportunity just in case it pays

indicators.note: around says the switch positions are placed either side of the article

parts.note: a switch can be set at on or at off
the is the definite article
a chance is an opportunity

explanation.surface: Someone flicks a switch round an article, hoping a chance pays off.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in the slim hope that it may work out is an idiom meaning just in case it pays.

clue.text: Balmoral, perhaps, is top property

parts.note: the head is the top of something
gear means belongings or property

explanation.surface: Balmoral Castle, the royal Scottish home, is top property.
explanation.walkthrough: A balmoral is also a flat Scottish bonnet, not only the royal castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A balmoral is a Scottish brimless cap, an example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: A medic heads for battle unit — fallen treated in this?

definitions.text: A medic heads for battle unit — fallen treated in this?

indicators.note: treated, as in processed or worked on, says the gathered letters are rearranged
heads for takes the first letters of battle and unit

explanation.surface: A doctor rushes to a front-line unit where the fallen are treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a medic does head there, and the wounded are treated in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile medical unit near the front line treats wounded soldiers, so the fallen are treated in it.

clue.text: Soldier in pub is definitely coherent

indicators.note: in says the soldier sits inside the pub

parts.note: the local is one's neighbourhood pub
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a pub insists he is perfectly coherent.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear reasoning that follows soundly is coherent through and through.

clue.text: Rest against involving British in Middle Eastern region

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the British letter goes inside

parts.note: lean on means rest against

explanation.surface: Britain leaning on a Middle Eastern region in diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: This country on the eastern Mediterranean coast lies in the Middle East.

clue.text: Flaming sailor: idle!

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to laze is to idle

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a lazy sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flaming' reads as a mild curse but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burning fiercely is on fire, alight and flaming.

clue.text: Billions always pull round a large corporation

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

indicators.note: round says the word for pull is turned the other way

parts.note: to tug is to pull

explanation.surface: A big business always pulls in billions.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is an old word for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a jocular old word for a big belly, and a drinker's paunch is a large one.

clue.text: Turned out I'd been right to have children within the family

definitions.text: to have children within the family

indicators.note: turned out means reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they had been right to keep children in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Mating closely related individuals produces offspring within one family line.

clue.text: Means of cutting government revenues centrally

indicators.note: centrally means only the middle of the word is used, its two ends dropped

parts.note: taxes are the government's revenues

explanation.surface: A news story about cutting government tax revenues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centrally' removes the outer letters of TAXES. The axe is also the slang for spending cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopping tool is a means of cutting wood, and the word also means budget cuts.

clue.text: Order minister to tender for NHS services

parts.note: to charge someone is to order or command them
to nurse someone is to minister to them

explanation.surface: A minister is ordered to put NHS services out to tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' is not a bid but one who tends the sick. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior ward nurse is a carer, one who tends patients, working in the National Health Service.

clue.text: Criticise cover when missing wicket

indicators.note: missing says the cricket letter is left out

parts.note: to wrap is to cover
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at cover is criticised when a wicket is missed.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is also a fielding position in cricket, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To rap someone is to rebuke or criticise them sharply.

clue.text: Wanting volume cut, annoyed about ringing of bell being magnified

indicators.note: about says the trimmed annoyance word goes round the bell sound
wanting means lacking, so the volume letter is missing from the word for annoyed

parts.note: vexed means annoyed
a toll is the slow ringing of a bell

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by a loud bell wants the volume turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' means lacking and drops V, leaving EXED; 'cut' only serves the surface. 'Magnified' is used in its old sense of praised, as in the Magnificat.
explanation.definitionFit: To be praised highly is to be glorified, and magnified is an old word for that.

clue.text: Gunman is discontented about missing number six

indicators.note: about says the shortened word is turned backwards
missing number six drops the sixth letter of the word

parts.note: repines means frets or is discontented

explanation.surface: A gunman is unhappy about losing number six, perhaps a teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing number six' drops the sixth letter, E, from REPINES, leaving REPINS; 'about' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman who shoots from a hidden position is a type of gunman.
